NVDA’s FY23 results show a company in transition: headline revenue is stabilizing sequentially (+2% QoQ) but still in a downcycle versus the 2022 peak (-21% YoY), consistent with digestion across consumer/PC end-markets. The key offset is mix: Data Center is ~60% of Q4 revenue and grew +11% YoY, with FY Data Center up +41% to $15B—an important divergence from the consolidated “pause” (FY revenue flat). Versus peers, this positions NVDA relatively well where spending is concentrating (AI infrastructure), supported by strong ecosystem signals (e.g., MSFT’s rapid Azure OpenAI adoption) and NVDA’s step-function performance claims for H100 vs A100 (training up to 9x; inference up to 30x), which can sustain pricing power and share.

Bearish factors are primarily timing and geopolitics: management flags hyperscaler demand timing risk, and China-related data center exposure adds uncertainty. Gaming remains the clear drag (Q4 -46% YoY; FY -27%), and the multi-quarter trajectory still reflects a sharp step-down from 2022 with only modest stabilization—suggesting the stock’s near-term trading will be driven more by Data Center order cadence than broad-based recovery.

Macro is mixed for risk assets: inflation is moderating but policy remains restrictive (Fed funds ~5.33%, 10Y ~4.44%), which can amplify volatility and compress multiples if growth disappoints. Trading signal: constructive on AI-led re-acceleration, but expect lumpiness; favor pullbacks unless Data Center re-accelerates QoQ.

NVDA’s 2024-Q1 prints a clear “AI-led rebound with consumer drag.” Total revenue of $7.19B rose +19% QoQ but remains -13% YoY, signaling recovery off a trough rather than a full-cycle re-acceleration back above the prior peak run-rate. The key offset is mix: Data Center at $4.28B grew +18% QoQ and +14% YoY, breaking out of the ~$3.6–$3.8B band seen through 2023 and aligning with peer indicators of sustained enterprise AI buildout (e.g., AMZN cloud growth and MSFT platform expansion). By contrast, Gaming at $2.24B is still -38% YoY despite a +22% QoQ bounce—consistent with a lingering PC/consumer digestion cycle and a relative weak spot versus peers’ broader top-line momentum.

Trading signals skew toward “buy on AI strength, respect macro/risk.” Bullish factors: accelerating Data Center trajectory, product/performance claims that reinforce platform leadership (throughput +20%, efficiency gains, RTX value/perf), and peer commentary supporting durable GenAI demand. Bearish factors: overall revenue still below prior highs, pronounced Gaming YoY decline, and explicit softness in general-purpose CPU infrastructure demand—an important watch item for near-term order volatility.

Macro is mixed: inflation ~3% and low unemployment support demand, but restrictive rates (Fed ~5.33%, yields ~4.16%) can pressure multiples and capex timing, increasing sensitivity to any demand wobble. Net: constructive bias driven by Data Center momentum, with elevated risk from cyclicality and rate-driven valuation compression.

Net: bullish on trend and peer leadership, tactically watch guidance follow-through and export headlines.

NVDA exits FY2024 with exceptional top-line strength and clear AI-infrastructure dominance: Q4 revenue of $22.1B (+22% QoQ, +265% YoY) and FY revenue of $60.9B (+126% YoY) are far beyond typical mega-cap growth profiles. That’s not bearish by itself, but it raises the bar for upside surprises and increases valuation/expectations risk. Positively, management’s prior $20B guide vs $22.1B delivery suggests conservative guidance, and product cadence (Spectrum‑X now; H200 shipments in Q2) supports continued demand capture. Expanding software/services ($1B run-rate) and networking (> $13B run-rate) add durability to the platform story.

Key bearish overhang is geopolitical: China is mid-single-digit Data Center mix, but no export licenses for restricted products limits optionality and can create headline volatility. Macro (rates ~4.65%, yields ~4.28%) is not restrictive enough to derail AI capex near-term, but it does penalize long-duration multiples.
